The petitioners, who are plaintiffs before the trial Court have called into question the correctness of the order dated 06.03.2019 passed on I.A.No.22 in O.S.No.457/2013 by the Court of II Addl. Senior Civil Judge and C.J.M., Mysuru, whereby the trial Court has rejected the application filed seeking amendment of the plaint.

sentences.text: 2. The parties are referred to by their ranks before the trial Court for the purpose of convenience.

3. The plaintiffs have filed a suit for partition and separate possession of their share in the suit 'A'
schedule properties and also in the amount kept with the defendant No.26 and have also sought for 3/7th share in suit 'B' schedule property.

4. What is of relevance in the present petition is that suit 'A' schedule property consists of the land Smt. J. Manjula vs Smt. Madamma on 8 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134319001/
6 bearing Sy.No.128/1A measuring 2 acres 17 guntas at Srirampura Village, Kasaba Hobli, Mysore Taluk.
5.
The suit has been filed by the daughters of late T.Javaraiah.
The respondents, who are defendants are the wife and sons of late T.Javaraiah.
The respondent Nos.26 to 31 who are defendant Nos.20 to 25 are children of late T.Venkataiah.

6. The facts that are of relevance insofar as the application is concerned is that, in the plaint, the plaintiffs had averred regarding the property in Item No.1 of suit 'A' schedule property as having been acquired by defendant No.26 for the purpose of distribution of house sites.
At para-6 of the plaint, it was specifically averred that the defendants are trying to take the compensation amount on the premise that the property exclusively belongs to late T.Venkataiah.

It is further asserted that the property has been purchased for the benefit of joint family and is not the self-acquired property and that the plaintiffs and - 10 - defendant Nos.1 to 25 are having common right and interests over the same.

7. In the written statement filed by defendant Nos.16 to 25, they had taken a specific stand that the subject matter of suit 'A' schedule property at Item No.1 is not the ancestral property and was self-acquired property of late Sri Venkataiah, which was granted by the Land Tribunal under the Inams Abolition Act.

8. It was further asserted at para-2 that the brother of T.Thimmaiah had filed a suit for similar relief against defendant Nos.16 to 25 and had failed to prove his case as regards the claim of one-third share in the suit schedule property in O.S.No.512/1990 and that the said finding has attained finality in the appeal proceedings in R.A.No.349/2009 and R.S.A.No.1730/2010.
9.
During the course of proceedings, an application for amendment has been filed by the plaintiffs.

The proposed amendment at para-5(a) reads as follows:-
- 11 - SCHEDULE Item No.1:-
After para 5 new para 5(a) may kindly be inserted which is as follows:-
5(a) As stated above T.Venkataiah, T.Javaraiah and T.Thimmaiah are brothers by full blood and members of an Hindu undivided family.
T.Venkataiah being the eldest Male member of the family was managing the affairs of the joint family.

In the capacity of the Karta and manager of the joint family and also for an on behalf of the joint family the late T. Venkataiah applied grant of occupancy rights in relation to Item No.1 of the suit schedule property that is land bearing Sy.No.128/1 measuring 2 acre 17 guntas situated at Srirampura village Kasaba Hobli Mysuru Taluk, Mysuru.

Smt. J. Manjula vs Smt. Madamma on 8 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134319001/
7
The application was registered in case number KLRM 182 clubbed with other applications by the land tribunal Mysuru.
After holding detailed enquiry the land tribunal granted occupancy rights the copy of which is herewith produced.

Hence it is submitted that though occupancy rights are granted individual name of T. Venkataiah it is for and on behalf of joint family comprising of the three brothers and hence item No.1 of the suit schedule property is the joint family property.

The same was treated as joint family property and at division that took place 11.12.1966 since the property was being jointly cultivated by the three brothers and among the three brothers and the - 12 - undivided 1/3rd share located in the northern side in item No.1 of the suit schedule property fell to the share of T.Javaraiah father of the Plaintiffs.
Thus Item No.1 of the suit schedule property is the coparcenary property in which the Plaintiffs have right by birth to claim share.

It is further submitted that the lease in respect of the Item No.1 of the suit schedule property was granted by the late Maharaja of Mysuru His Highness Sri Sri Sri Mummadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar Thereafter, this land was being jointly cultivated by three brothers.
10.

A perusal of afore-extracted para-5(a) would indicate the stand of plaintiffs that the land in Item No.1 of suit schedule property which is Survey No.128/1A at Srirampura Village was subject-matter of claim before the Land Tribunal and the occupancy rights were granted after enquiry.

It is asserted that though occupancy rights were granted in the individual name of T.Venkataiah, such grant was for the benefit of the joint family comprising of three brothers and accordingly, Item No.1 of suit schedule property is a joint family property.
It is this proposed amendment which is objected to by the defendants.

. The trial Court has rejected the application while observing that the evidence of plaintiffs' side was concluded and PW-1 was fully cross-examined and that the additional documents have been permitted to be produced and that the plaintiffs were seeking to take a different stand from the one that is put forth earlier that Item No.1 of suit schedule property was purchased by their grandfather and in the proposed amendment were now pleading as regards Item No.1 of suit schedule propertiy that the occupancy rights granted in favour of late T.Venkataiah was the grant for the benefit of entire family.

12. The trial court has referred to the evidence of PW-1 on 02.09.2015 who had deposed for the first time that the suit schedule property was purchased by her grandfather T.Thimmaiah though she did not know from whom and when he had purchased the same.
The trial Court has further referred to her stand that she had not produced any proof before the Court in that regard.

sentences.text: trial Court has further noticed that the stand of plaintiff- PW1 during her evidence that she had pleaded ignorance regarding the proceedings initiated by Sri Ningaiah regarding the grant of occupancy rights.

13. The trial Court has also noticed that the suit was of the year 2013 and the plaintiff had kept quiet for all these years till the fag end of proceedings and it has also observed that the plaintiffs were intending to add new set of facts and evidence, which is contrary to law.
14. Heard both sides.
15. Sri A.Madhusudana Rao, learned counsel for the petitioners had contended that the stand taken insofar as the said Item No.1 of Sy.No.128/1A was specifically that it was a joint family property.

The fact that the proposed amendment recites regarding the acquisition of right through occupancy, it is submitted would not make a difference, as the stand that nature of property being a joint family property remains the same.

. It is further submitted that the fact that the application was filed after commencement of trial and should not be rejected by relying on the Proviso to Order VI Rule 17 of C.P.C. invoking the requirement of due diligence, as that by itself would not be bar.

17. Sri G.V.Chandrashekar, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of Ms.Apeksha.D and Sri Suhas.S for respondent Nos.26 to 31 on the other hand submits that in the written statement, a specific stand is taken regarding the property in Sy.No.128/1A being the land granted by Land Tribunal in KLRM. INA-39/81-82 and had further narrated the manner of consideration of right of occupancy rights and its challenge by one Ningaiah.

18. It is further submitted that these matters were also subject matter of adjudication at the instance of other brother of Thimmaiah, who had filed a suit for similar relief in O.S.No.512/1990 which had attained finality and accordingly, it is asserted that these facts relating to conferment of occupancy rights were matter of record and - 16 - the plaintiffs in the present suit could not have been oblivious to such tracing of title and the application filed in the suit of the year 2013, i.e. after more than six years of progress of the proceedings ought not to be permitted and application ought to be rejected as there was no due diligence.
19.
It must be noticed that admittedly, the suit is filed by the daughters of late T.Javaraiah claiming partition.

The rights with respect to Item No.1 in Survey No.128/1A was subject matter of adjudication in O.S.No.512/1990 between T.Thimmaiah, the brother of late T.Javaraiah and other family members, including late T.Javaraiah, who was defendant No.2 through whom the plaintiffs Smt. J. Manjula vs Smt. Madamma on 8 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134319001/
9 claim.
20.
It must be noticed that O.S.No.512/1990 filed by T.Thimmaiah came to be dismissed and the matter was taken up in R.A.No.349/2009.

Insofar as Item No.1 in Survey No.128/1A is concerned,
there is a specific finding at para-18 in R.A.No.349/2009 that, wherein, the Court - 17 - had observed that the property which is Item No.1 in the present suit was the self-acquired property of defendant No.1 in the said suit, i.e. T.Venkataiah.

The relevant extract of para-18 in R.A.No.349/2009 reads as hereunder:-
"18. ...
Evidence available on record goes to show that the suit property is the self-acquired property of the defendant No.1....
On the other hand the LR's of the defendant No.1 proves that suit schedule property was the self acquired property of defendant No.1...."

21 . Though in the present proceedings the trial Court is deciding the amendment application and the Court ought not to readily enter into the merits of the claim, however, the observations and findings made in the previous proceedings may have a bearing as to whether the amendment sought for could have been filed at an earlier stage to reflect due diligence.
Subsequent to the amendment of Order VI Rule 17 of C.P.C., the aspect of diligence is a matter that requires to be considered.

- 18 - That the amendment has the effect of reflecting a change in stance of the parties after the proceedings have progressed and after definitive stand is taken in the evidence by the parties, is also an aspect to be kept in mind.

22. It must be seen that insofar as tracing of title is concerned, when admittedly the plaintiffs are tracing their title through late T.Javaraiah and the manner in which late T.Javaraiah had title to the property, is a matter of investigation that ought to have been done before the suit was filed.

If that were to be so and in light of the findings by the Appellate Court in R.A.No.849/2009 at para-18, this fact of tracing of title and the stand including regarding the conferment of occupancy rights in favour of Venkataiah ought to have been made at the very initial stage of filing of the plaint.
23.
It is the matter of record that in the plaint what is only mentioned insofar as the land at Survey No.128/1A - 19 - is that the same had been purchased for the benefit of joint family.

In the evidence of PW-1, it is also a matter of record that the trial Court has referred to the evidence of PW-1 and the stand taken by PW-1 that suit 'A' schedule property was purchased by her grandfather T.Thimmaiah and the Smt. J. Manjula vs Smt. Madamma on 8 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134319001/
10
plaintiff did not know from whom it was purchased.

Insofar as the suggestion regarding the proceedings relating to occupancy rights and that the said proceedings culminated in Venkataiah being the owner of Item No.1 of suit 'A' schedule property as well, PW1 had pleaded ignorance.

24. The answers of PW1 elicited in the cross- examination as is relevant is extracted hereinbelow:-
"...The said property was purchased by my grandfather - T.Thimmaiah but I do not know from whom and when he has purchased the same.
I have not produced any such document before the Court.
It is not true to suggest that I am deposing false and the said property belongs to T.Venkataiah.

I do not know there was one proceedings initiated (sic) at the instance of one - 20 - Ningaiah for occupancy rights and the said matter went upto High Court and declare (sic) that T.Venkataiah was the owner of the Item no.1 of the plaint 'A' schedule...."

25. In light of the specific finding that this Item No.1 of Sy. No.128/1A was the self-acquired property of Venkataiah in terms of the observations made at para-18 of the judgment in Regular Appeal least that was expected of the plaintiffs was to take a stand with reference to the findings in the earlier proceedings.

No doubt, the Court does not intend to record a finding regarding the binding nature or otherwise of observations made in the previous proceedings or whether it would amount to res judicata in the present proceedings, but nonetheless, due diligence that was required was to place before the Court while filing of the plaint, the status of earlier proceedings and the position of deriving of title insofar as Item No.1.
The plaintiff has not made out exercise of due diligence in seeking for amendment after trial had commenced.

. It is in this regard, the stand of plaintiffs by way of proposed amendment to now contend that grant of occupancy rights was for the benefit of the family is obviously an attempt to salvage the case after definitive stand was taken in the evidence that she was not aware of the grant of occupancy rights.
27.

The affidavit filed in support of the application is also bald, though normally the Court would be liberal insofar as amendment application is concerned, in the peculiar case, judicial discretion to allow the application for amendment cannot be exercised due to absence of diligence in seeking for amendment before commencement of trial, this would be so both in light of finding in para-18 of R.A.No.349/2009 in previous round of proceedings as well as an attempt to change in stance after PW1 in his evidence has taken a specific stand of ignorance insofar as conferment of occupancy rights is concerned.

- 22 - Smt. J. Manjula vs Smt. Madamma on 8 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134319001/

The petition is rejected.

29. It is clarified that the observations made in this order are only for the limited purpose of disposing of the application for amendment and the same is not to be construed to be a binding finding regarding the merits of the matter which is subject to trial.

opennyai_summary.facts:
2. The parties are referred to by their ranks before the trial Court for the purpose of convenience.
3. The plaintiffs have filed a suit for partition and separate possession of their share in the suit 'A'
schedule properties and also in the amount kept with the defendant No.26 and have also sought for 3/7th share in suit 'B' schedule property.
It is further asserted that the property has been purchased for the benefit of joint family and is not the self-acquired property and that the plaintiffs and - 10 - defendant Nos.1 to 25 are having common right and interests over the same.
7. In the written statement filed by defendant Nos.16 to 25, they had taken a specific stand that the subject matter of suit 'A' schedule property at Item No.1 is not the ancestral property and was self-acquired property of late Sri Venkataiah, which was granted by the Land Tribunal under the Inams Abolition Act.
T.Venkataiah being the eldest Male member of the family was managing the affairs of the joint family.
The same was treated as joint family property and at division that took place 11.12.1966 since the property was being jointly cultivated by the three brothers and among the three brothers and the - 12 - undivided 1/3rd share located in the northern side in item No.1 of the suit schedule property fell to the share of T.Javaraiah father of the Plaintiffs.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It must be noticed that admittedly, the suit is filed by the daughters of late T.Javaraiah claiming partition.
The rights with respect to Item No.1 in Survey No.128/1A was subject matter of adjudication in O.S.No.512/1990 between T.Thimmaiah, the brother of late T.Javaraiah and other family members, including late T.Javaraiah, who was defendant No.2 through whom the plaintiffs Smt. J. Manjula vs Smt. Madamma on 8 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134319001/
9 claim.
20.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It must be noticed that O.S.No.512/1990 filed by T.Thimmaiah came to be dismissed and the matter was taken up in R.A.No.349/2009.
21 . Though in the present proceedings the trial Court is deciding the amendment application and the Court ought not to readily enter into the merits of the claim, however, the observations and findings made in the previous proceedings may have a bearing as to whether the amendment sought for could have been filed at an earlier stage to reflect due diligence.
Subsequent to the amendment of Order VI Rule 17 of C.P.C., the aspect of diligence is a matter that requires to be considered.
- 18 - That the amendment has the effect of reflecting a change in stance of the parties after the proceedings have progressed and after definitive stand is taken in the evidence by the parties, is also an aspect to be kept in mind.
22. It must be seen that insofar as tracing of title is concerned, when admittedly the plaintiffs are tracing their title through late T.Javaraiah and the manner in which late T.Javaraiah had title to the property, is a matter of investigation that ought to have been done before the suit was filed.
If that were to be so and in light of the findings by the Appellate Court in R.A.No.849/2009 at para-18, this fact of tracing of title and the stand including regarding the conferment of occupancy rights in favour of Venkataiah ought to have been made at the very initial stage of filing of the plaint.
23.
No doubt, the Court does not intend to record a finding regarding the binding nature or otherwise of observations made in the previous proceedings or whether it would amount to res judicata in the present proceedings, but nonetheless, due diligence that was required was to place before the Court while filing of the plaint, the status of earlier proceedings and the position of deriving of title insofar as Item No.1.
The plaintiff has not made out exercise of due diligence in seeking for amendment after trial had commenced.
The affidavit filed in support of the application is also bald, though normally the Court would be liberal insofar as amendment application is concerned, in the peculiar case, judicial discretion to allow the application for amendment cannot be exercised due to absence of diligence in seeking for amendment before commencement of trial, this would be so both in light of finding in para-18 of R.A.No.349/2009 in previous round of proceedings as well as an attempt to change in stance after PW1 in his evidence has taken a specific stand of ignorance insofar as conferment of occupancy rights is concerned.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, this Court does not find any ground to interfere with the order of the trial Court.
The petition is rejected.
